learning_objectives: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\"><strong>Assertion (A) :<\/strong> Frictional force is the component of contact force parallel to the surface.<br \/>\n<strong>Reason (R) :<\/strong> Friction force always opposes the motion of a body.<br \/>\nIn the light of the above statements

text_solutions.text:
"
1. Question Explanation:
We are asked to analyze two statements:
  • Assertion (A): Friction is the component of contact force parallel to the surface.
  • Reason (R): Friction opposes the motion of a body. The goal is to determine if both statements are true and whether Reason explains Assertion.
2. Concept Based:
  • Friction: Friction is a force that resists the relative motion of two surfaces in contact. This force is always parallel to the surface and is part of the contact force.
  • Opposition of Motion: Friction resists the relative motion of objects. It acts in the opposite direction of the motion or the tendency of motion between surfaces in contact.
3. Formula Used:
The frictional force fff is given by:
f=µΝ
where:
  • µ is the coefficient of friction (static or kinetic),
  • N is the normal (perpendicular) force,
  • Friction always acts parallel to the contact surface.
4. Analysis:
  • Assertion (A): True. Friction is indeed a component of the contact force that acts parallel to the surface, opposing relative motion.
  • Reason (R): False. Friction always opposes the relative motion (or the tendency of motion) between two surfaces in contact. It does not necessarily oppose the motion of the body as a whole, but rather the motion of the surfaces relative to each other.
However, Reason (R) does not explain why friction is parallel to the surface, which is the c9re idea in Assertion (A).
Conclusion:
The correct answer is Option 4 (A) is true but (R) is false.
"

learning_objectives: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">When a tetraploid female plant is crossed with a diploid male plant
the ploidy of endosperm cells in resulting seed of this angiosperm would be:<\/div>\n"

text_solutions.text:
"

Explain Question : The question asks to identify Ploidy of the endosperm resulting from a tetraploid female x diploid male cross.

Concept : This question is based on the concept of Double Fertilization in angiosperms (flowering plants).

Solution : The endosperm (3n) forms from the fusion of one male gamete (n→2n/2=n) and two polar nuclei (2n→n+n).

  • Female plant: Tetraploid (4n). Polar nuclei are 2n+2n=4n.

  • Male plant: Diploid (2n). Male gamete is n.
    Endosperm ploidy = n (male gamete) + 2n (polar nuclei) + 2n (polar nuclei) =∗∗5n∗∗ (Pentaploidy).
    *Correction based on typical ploidy rules:

  • Female (4n) → Egg (2n), Polar nuclei (2n,2n) (Unfused).

  • Male (2n) → Male gamete (n).

Endosperm fusion: Male gamete (n) + Polar nuclei (2n) + Polar nuclei (2n) → 5n (Pentaploidy).

Final Answer : option (1) Pentaploidy
"
"Ploidy of endosperm in angiosperm =  × ploidy of male plant + Ploidy of female plant"
